key_insight: QuantiSpect replaces dense 3D convolutions with factorized, structure-aware branches to achieve a lighter surface-code pre-decoder without sacrificing decoding performance.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to lower-latency, lower-memory quantum error correction for scalable fault-tolerant hardware.
method: Uses a 3-branch residual block: depthwise spatial, depthwise temporal, and grouped spatio-temporal convolutions.
Adds squeeze-and-excitation channel gating to emphasize useful syndrome features.
Builds on the rotated surface code decoding pipeline of Chamberland et al. and targets a neural pre-decoder stage.
evidence_signal: On a unified 4×A100 benchmark, the model matched the Accurate baseline at R=13 with ~2.71× fewer parameters and ~2.84× fewer MACs, while preserving threshold/accuracy at moderate and large distances.
watch_item: The gains depend on careful hardware-aware deployment and benchmark conditions, so real decoder latency and robustness still need validation on target quantum control stacks.
paper_title: QuantiSpect: A Structure-Aware Lightweight 3D CNN Pre-Decoder for Scalable Surface Code Quantum Error Correction
